We aim to develop innovative, practical solutions to real-world challenges using NASA's open data. We welcome enthusiastic members with skills in programming, astronomy, data science, UI/UX, GIS, research, and creative problem-solving.
summary:
FIRELINK is an interactive satellite fire-monitoring and harmonization platform developed by Team CORE SIGNAL to address inconsistencies between MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations. Differences in sensor sensitivity, spatial resolution and observation characteristics can create artificial jumps in long-term hotspot records, making it difficult to distinguish actual changes in fire activity from changes in satellite detection capabilities.

FIRELINK addresses this challenge through a common-detectability harmonization approach rather than artificially scaling one sensor's observations upward. It provides tools to explore fire activity, examine detection patterns, investigate calibration behaviour and compare correction methods through a sensor-transition benchmark. The framework also incorporates observation gaps, held-out validation and uncertainty reporting to make its results more transparent.

By helping researchers identify and measure artificial discontinuities in satellite-derived fire records, FIRELINK aims to support more reliable long-term fire analysis, environmental monitoring and interpretation of changing fire patterns. Its interactive interface makes complex satellite-data comparisons easier to explore and understand.
details:
FIRELINK – Harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS Active-Fire Observations

FIRELINK is an interactive satellite-data analysis platform designed to improve the comparability of long-term active-fire records from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS instruments. These sensors differ in spatial resolution, sensitivity, and observation characteristics. As a result, a change in the number of detected hotspots may sometimes reflect a change in the observing satellite rather than a genuine change in fire activity.

FIRELINK addresses this challenge through a common-detectability harmonization approach. Instead of artificially increasing the detection capability of the less-sensitive sensor, the platform aims to compare observations at a common level of detectability. Its workflow includes fire-observation exploration, threshold-based comparison, residual calibration, sensor-transition benchmarking, and uncertainty reporting.

The platform provides an interactive interface through which users can explore fire activity, examine sensor differences, investigate calibration behaviour, and compare alternative correction approaches. It also considers missing observations and the limitations of available data so that unobserved areas are not automatically interpreted as areas without fire.

The intended impact is to help researchers, environmental analysts, and decision-makers interpret long-term fire patterns more reliably. By identifying potential artificial discontinuities in satellite-derived fire records, FIRELINK aims to support more consistent wildfire analysis and environmental monitoring.

Technology and tools: Python, JavaScript, React, Vite, FastAPI, and data-processing and visualization libraries. The project uses a web-based architecture with a Python backend and an interactive frontend.

Creativity and innovation: FIRELINK focuses not only on displaying fire hotspots but also on investigating whether differences between satellite sensors introduce artificial changes into long-term records. Its sensor-transition benchmark compares different harmonization approaches, while its emphasis on uncertainty and data provenance helps users understand the reliability and limitations of the results.

The team considered sensor resolution, detection sensitivity, observation timing, data availability, missing observations, calibration bias, uncertainty, validation, and the risk of presenting synthetic or incomplete data as actual satellite observations.
